author: reek
body: The MQTT client endpoint driven end to end with no network. The broker side is built with the Mqtt codec, so the endpoint under test is reading real MQTT v5 packets rather than talking to itself.

author: reek
body: Built with the codec, not with the endpoint, so the two halves do not share a code path.

author: reek
body: EACH SCENARIO GETS ITS OWN ENDPOINT, and that is a requirement rather than tidiness. `MqttEp` is threaded linearly like every other endpoint in this tree: `__record-set` stores into the record and returns the SAME one, so a value that has been handed onward is spent. Written the obvious way -- two subscriptions branching off one connected endpoint -- the second call mutates the state the first still refers to, and the assertions read a record neither scenario owns. That is what the first run of this test did, and it reported a wrong answer for two scenarios at once.
